h1: The 6 Best Cordless Electric Kettles With Auto Shutoff of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Electric Kettles: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 cordless electric kettles with auto shutoff compared on capacity, wattage, interior material, lid and boil-dry protection.
mainKeyword: cordless electric kettles with auto shutoff
summary: The Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter is the best kettle for most kitchens, with 1500 watts, a stainless body, auto shutoff and boil-dry protection under $25. The Cosori keeps plastic out of the water path, the COMFEE' has a 304 steel interior, the Chefman is the glass pick for bigger batches, and the 1 liter Hamilton Beach is the lightest to pour.
intro: Auto shutoff is the feature every kettle listing promises and the one that matters least in a good kettle. A switch that stops the boil is table stakes. What separates the good ones is where the water touches plastic, how wide the mouth is for cleaning, and whether the lid opens far enough to scrub scale off the element.

We ranked six kettles from the listings: capacity, wattage, interior material, lid and mouth design, safety features and weight. The cordless part means the kettle lifts off a base to pour, which is the standard design here, with one model that stresses cord-free serving. Wattage sets boil speed, so a 1100 watt kettle is slower than a 1500 watt one.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter Electric Tea Kettle
products.verdict: A 1.7 liter, 1500 watt stainless kettle with auto shutoff, boil-dry protection and a power light.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter has a stainless steel body, 1500 watts of power, auto shutoff, boil-dry protection and an indicator light that shows when it is on.

It ranks first because the listing covers both safety features and does so at the under $25 bracket, with the same wattage as the pricier kettles. It beats the OVENTE on power, 1500 against 1100 watts, so it boils faster. The compromise is that it does not promise a plastic-free water path like the Cosori.

Buy it if you want strong power and plain controls. Skip it if you want zero plastic touching the water. It is the benchmark the others are measured against.
products.idealFor: Households that want a plain, strong stainless kettle.
products.skipIf: You want no plastic in the water path.

products.name: Cosori Electric Kettle, No Plastic Contact, 1.7L
products.verdict: A 1.7 liter kettle where no plastic touches the water, with a wide mouth and a large-angle lid.
products.description:
The Cosori has a 1.7 liter capacity, no plastic contact with water, a wide mouth and a large-angle lid, and heats 0.5 liters in under 3 minutes.

It ranks second because the wide mouth and large-angle lid make descaling easy, and the no-plastic claim matters for taste. It trails the Hamilton Beach on price and on the safety features the listing names. Heating 0.5 liters in under 3 minutes is a fast result for a cup or two.

Buy it if you make a cup or two at a time and clean often. Skip it if you want the lowest price. The wide mouth is a real advantage in hard water areas.
cons: Costs more than the Hamilton Beach
products.idealFor: People who make one or two cups at a time.

products.name: COMFEE' Stainless Steel Electric Kettle 1.7 Liter
products.verdict: A 1.7 liter, 1500 watt kettle with a 304 food-grade steel interior and a concealed element.
products.description:
The COMFEE' has a 304 food-grade steel inner pot, 1500 watts, a concealed heating element, an LED indicator and a removable lid.

It ranks third because the concealed element wipes clean, and 304 steel is a respected grade. It sits below the Cosori because it does not claim a plastic-free path. The listing does not itemize auto shutoff, which most kettles include.

Buy it if you want a steel interior and easy cleaning. Skip it if you want a documented shutoff feature. Check the lid hinge for easy cleaning.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want a steel interior and a smooth element.

products.name: Chefman Electric Kettle 1.8L 1500W Glass
products.verdict: A 1.8 liter, 1500 watt glass kettle with a removable lid and boil-dry protection.
products.description:
The Chefman has a 1.8 liter capacity, 1500 watts, a glass body, a removable lid and boil-dry protection.

It ranks fourth because glass lets you see the water level and any scale, and 1.8 liters is the biggest here. Glass is heavier and more fragile than steel, and more breakable if dropped.

Buy it if you want to see the water and brew bigger batches. Skip it if the kettle will be handled by children. Handle it gently, as glass chips at the spout.
products.idealFor: Households that want to see the water level.
products.skipIf: The kettle will be knocked around.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1 Liter Electric Tea Kettle
products.verdict: A 1 liter cord-free kettle with auto shutoff, boil-dry protection and a rapid-boil system.
products.description:
The 1 liter Hamilton Beach stresses cord-free serving, auto shutoff, boil-dry protection and a rapid-boil system.

It ranks fifth because 1 liter is small for a family, but it is the lightest to lift full. It suits a single drinker or a desk.

Buy it if you drink alone or have limited strength. Skip it if you serve a pot of tea. Keep it on a stable counter near the outlet.

products.skipIf: You make tea for several people.

products.verdict: A 1.7 liter, 1100 watt stainless kettle that is BPA-free.
products.description:
The OVENTE has a 1.7 liter capacity, 1100 watts, a stainless steel body, a BPA-free build and a black finish.

It ranks last because 1100 watts is the slowest here, and the listing does not detail safety features. It still holds a full 1.7 liters.

Buy it if you can accept a slower boil. Skip it if speed or safety listings matter. It is the budget way to a full 1.7 liters, if you can wait on the boil.

whatMatters.detail: Auto shutoff turns the kettle off when the water boils, which protects the element and the kitchen. Almost every kettle includes it, but only some listings say so. Look for the words auto shutoff and boil-dry protection on the page, which are two separate safeguards. It is worth reading closely, because a kettle without boil-dry protection can damage the element if switched on empty.

Wattage sets how quickly a kettle boils. 1500 watts is the common high end, and the OVENTE's 1100 watts is slower. Check the number on the listing, since the difference is the minute you stand waiting for a morning cup. A faster kettle also uses less total energy per cup, since it spends less time losing heat to the room.

The inside is what touches your water. Stainless steel, 304 steel and glass are common, and some kettles include plastic parts that can influence taste. Check the interior material, and look for no plastic contact if you drink plain hot water. Taste is the quiet giveaway, especially in a new kettle that smells of plastic for the first few boils.

1 liter suits a single drinker, 1.7 liters covers a small family and 1.8 liters is the largest here. A bigger kettle is heavier when full. Check the capacity on the listing, and consider how much you lift at once. Fill lines on the inside help you boil only what you need.

Scale builds up inside any kettle over time. A wide mouth, large-angle lid or concealed element makes descaling quick. Look for these words on the listing, and be wary of a narrow neck that blocks a sponge. Plan to descale every month or two if you live in a hard water area.

faq.q: Do all kettles shut off by themselves?
faq.a: Most do, but the listings differ. The Hamilton Beach models and Chefman name auto shutoff or boil-dry protection, while the COMFEE', Cosori and OVENTE listings do not itemize them. Check the page. Always check the page for both features.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Ignoring the water path. A kettle can be stainless outside yet use plastic inside, which can flavor tea. The Cosori states no plastic contacts water, which settles it. A wide mouth also helps in hard water areas.

faq.q: Is the Cosori worth it over the Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter?
faq.a: If you clean often or care about taste, yes. The Cosori has a wide mouth and no plastic in the water path, but the Hamilton Beach has 1500 watts and named safety features for less. Check the base footprint on a small counter.

faq.q: How do I descale a kettle?
faq.a: Boil a mix of water and white vinegar, let it sit, then rinse well. A wide mouth like the Cosori's makes wiping easier, and a concealed element like the COMFEE's reduces scale traps. Unplug it before cleaning.

faq.q: How should I look after the base?
faq.a: Keep the base dry and wipe the contacts. Never submerge the base or the kettle's electric parts, and dry the glass Chefman to prevent water spots. Descaling also speeds up the next boil.

faq.q: Can I boil milk in a kettle?
faq.a: No. Kettles are for water, and milk scorches on the element and is hard to clean. Use a pot instead. Wash the lid by hand.

finalTake: The Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter Electric Tea Kettle is the best buy, with 1500 watts, a stainless body and named safety features under $25. Choose the Cosori if you want no plastic in the water, the COMFEE' for a 304 steel interior, and the Chefman if you like glass. The 1 liter Hamilton Beach is the lightest pour.
